correctness.rationale: The Haar-adjoint transfer maps the character at frequency k to the one at l exactly when k=(A^T)^n l. This is an orthogonal partial injection on normalized Fourier bases; its nonzero singular values are therefore the reciprocal frequency weights on the image sublattice. Commuting unimodularity makes that sublattice independent of m. For R squared equals 2I, the image lattices alternate between 2^j Z² and 2^j(Z×2Z), yielding both exact lists and the max norm. Matrix eigenvalues show the expansion contrast; lattice counting and dominated convergence establish the Schatten threshold and limits. The embedded exact-integer checker passed 51,623 finite lattice tests; unrestricted assertions rely on the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The exact full singular-value sequence, not only the leading norm, fails to distinguish an expanding degree-two toral endomorphism from countably many hyperbolic nonexpanding ones with arbitrarily large Lyapunov separation. This is a structural inverse-problem boundary for quantitative transfer smoothing. The parity-resolved Schatten phase constants and sharp p threshold further show what detailed smoothing information does and does not capture; it is not an arbitrary parameter recomputation.
